questions.subject: ANALYTICAL_CHEMISTRY
questions.learningObjective: identify pH at half-equivalence of a weak acid
questions.stem: Sample 1201: A weak monoprotic acid with pKa 7.92 is titrated with strong base. What is the pH at the half-equivalence point?

options.misconception: reports the pKb rather than the pH
adds one unit without a concentration basis
uses the strong acid equivalence result instead of the half-equivalence result

questions.explanation: At half-equivalence exactly half of the weak acid has been converted to conjugate base, so the base-to-acid ratio is one and its logarithm is zero. Henderson-Hasselbalch then reduces to pH equal to pKa.
questions.hint: At half-neutralization the ratio [base]/[acid] is one.

questions.subject: ANALYTICAL_CHEMISTRY
questions.learningObjective: estimate equivalence pH of a weak acid titration
questions.stem: Sample 1202: A weak acid with pKa 5.61 is titrated to equivalence with strong base, giving a salt concentration of 0.162 M. Estimate the pH at equivalence.

options.misconception: uses the neutral result valid only for strong acid titrations
uses the half-equivalence pH instead of the equivalence pH
applies the acidic hydrolysis expression with the wrong sign

questions.explanation: At equivalence the conjugate base of the weak acid hydrolyzes water to produce hydroxide. Using Kb equals Kw over Ka gives pH approximately seven plus one half of pKa plus the log of the salt concentration, which is above seven.
questions.hint: The conjugate base makes the equivalence point basic.

questions.stem: Sample 1237: A weak monoprotic acid with pKa 5.89 is titrated with strong base. What is the pH at the half-equivalence point?

options.misconception: adds one unit without a concentration basis
reports the pKb rather than the pH
uses the strong acid equivalence result instead of the half-equivalence result

questions.explanation: At half-equivalence exactly half of the weak acid has been converted to conjugate base, so the base-to-acid ratio is one and its logarithm is zero. Henderson-Hasselbalch then reduces to pH equal to pKa.
questions.hint: At half-neutralization the ratio [base]/[acid] is one.

questions.subject: ANALYTICAL_CHEMISTRY
questions.learningObjective: estimate equivalence pH of a weak acid titration
questions.stem: Sample 1238: A weak acid with pKa 5.06 is titrated to equivalence with strong base, giving a salt concentration of 0.113 M. Estimate the pH at equivalence.

options.misconception: uses the neutral result valid only for strong acid titrations
applies the acidic hydrolysis expression with the wrong sign
uses the half-equivalence pH instead of the equivalence pH

questions.explanation: At equivalence the conjugate base of the weak acid hydrolyzes water to produce hydroxide. Using Kb equals Kw over Ka gives pH approximately seven plus one half of pKa plus the log of the salt concentration, which is above seven.
questions.hint: The conjugate base makes the equivalence point basic.

questions.stem: Sample 1273: A weak monoprotic acid with pKa 3.94 is titrated with strong base. What is the pH at the half-equivalence point?

options.misconception: adds one unit without a concentration basis
uses the strong acid equivalence result instead of the half-equivalence result
reports the pKb rather than the pH

questions.explanation: At half-equivalence exactly half of the weak acid has been converted to conjugate base, so the base-to-acid ratio is one and its logarithm is zero. Henderson-Hasselbalch then reduces to pH equal to pKa.
questions.hint: At half-neutralization the ratio [base]/[acid] is one.

questions.subject: ANALYTICAL_CHEMISTRY
questions.learningObjective: estimate equivalence pH of a weak acid titration
questions.stem: Sample 1274: A weak acid with pKa 6.18 is titrated to equivalence with strong base, giving a salt concentration of 0.121 M. Estimate the pH at equivalence.

options.misconception: uses the neutral result valid only for strong acid titrations
applies the acidic hydrolysis expression with the wrong sign
uses the half-equivalence pH instead of the equivalence pH

questions.explanation: At equivalence the conjugate base of the weak acid hydrolyzes water to produce hydroxide. Using Kb equals Kw over Ka gives pH approximately seven plus one half of pKa plus the log of the salt concentration, which is above seven.
questions.hint: The conjugate base makes the equivalence point basic.
